title: Normalized morphism into recorded qcqs compact support
statement: Under the field, coefficient, finite-type and compactification hypotheses of [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], there is a unique natural morphism from the actual completed proper/open compact-support functor on integral constructible inputs to the recorded integral action [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action]. Its positive finite scalar reduction, followed by the recorded chosen projection adjunct, is the actual proper/open coefficient mate, in the canonical finiteReductionIso and finiteImageIso coordinates. No invertibility of this natural morphism is asserted. This is the simultaneous normalization of all objects and all levels.

source.place: Proof of sk-prop-scalar-six-compact-support; Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.6, 6.7.7 and 6.1.13; Stacks 0941 and 0F7J
source.note: Agent-stated proper/open realization prerequisite; proof details in module docstring.

proof.text: Take the hom of the normalized natural isomorphism supplied by lem-qcqs-compact-support-normalized-iso-existence. Its projection equations are exactly SfQcqsCompactSupportMorphismSpec. This separates existence and invertibility from the disputed rigidity assertion.

For any other normalized transformation, cancel the invertible recorded finite reduction isomorphism from the two normalization equations. All actual finite scalar reductions agree. Apply natural-transformation reduction rigidity, obtaining equality with tau and hence unique existence.

proof_origin.place: Existence portion of normalized lift; uniqueness remains the previous rigidity argument.

theorem sfQcqsCompactSupport_normalizedLift_existsUnique :

      sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor l K₀ hl c E ⋙
        (sfIntegralConstructible l E Y).ι,
      SfQcqsCompactSupportMorphismSpec l E K₀ hl c τ
